# FDS Draft: ST-1 Startup Sequence and Protection

Items marked **[TBC]** are not in the supplied data. They are placeholders to confirm with the turbine OEM or the Woodward application engineer.

## 1. Startup Sequence

### 1.1 Scope and control split
- The Woodward governor handles speed/load control, critical-band avoidance, the acceleration ramp, and the overspeed function.
- The DCS handles auxiliaries, permissives, step sequencing, and operator interface.
- Trip functions in section 2 are hardwired or in the Woodward/trip system. They must not depend on DCS availability.

### 1.2 Startup permissives (ready to start)
All of the following must be true to release the sequence:
1. No active trip, and the trip latch has been reset.
2. Lube oil header PT-210 ≥ 1.5 barg (normal) with P-11 running.
3. P-12 (emergency DC oil pump) in auto and DC supply healthy.
4. Turning gear M-15 running and the turbine at zero speed.
5. Cold start only: turning gear run time ≥ 2 h (timer in DCS, retained across a DCS restart **[TBC]**).
6. Condenser vacuum established: PT-220 below the alarm limit **[TBC]**, with the vacuum system in service.
7. Vibration XT-301/302 and thrust ZT-310 healthy (no bad-quality signals) and below alarm.
8. Steam supply conditions within the OEM start envelope **[TBC]**. Casing metal temperatures determine whether the start is cold or warm.
9. Generator breaker 52G open and auto-synchronizer available.

### 1.3 Sequence steps

| Step | Action | Exit condition |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Standby. Permissives are evaluated. | All permissives true and operator issues START. |
| 1 | Start P-11 if not already running. Confirm PT-210 at normal. | PT-210 ≥ 1.5 barg for a set time **[TBC]**. |
| 2 | Turning gear. Confirm M-15 running. For a cold start, run it for ≥ 2 h. Warm and hot starts follow the OEM minimum **[TBC]**. | Timer complete (cold). |
| 3 | Reset trip, open the trip/stop valve, and release the governor. | Stop valve open and no trip. |
| 4 | Roll-off. Governor ramps toward 500 rpm. M-15 disengages as speed rises (automatic overrunning clutch, or DCS-commanded disengage **[TBC]**) and is then stopped. | Speed ≥ 500 rpm and M-15 disengaged. |
| 5 | Warm-up hold 1: 500 rpm for 20 min (cold start only). Hold timer runs only while speed is within a tolerance band **[TBC]**. Check vibration, thrust, and bearing temperatures. | Timer elapsed and no alarms. |
| 6 | Accelerate to 2000 rpm. Pass through the 1600–1900 rpm critical band at the critical-pass acceleration rate **[TBC]**. | Speed ≥ 2000 rpm. |
| 7 | Warm-up hold 2: 2000 rpm for 15 min. | Timer elapsed and no alarms. |
| 8 | Accelerate to 3600 rpm. Switch the main oil supply to the shaft-driven pump. Confirm PT-210 stays normal. P-11 stays in auto-standby. | 3600 rpm stable and PT-210 ≥ 1.5 barg on the shaft pump. |
| 9 | Auto-sync. The Woodward matches speed and the synchronizer matches voltage, frequency, and phase. 52G closes through the auto-synchronizer and sync-check permissive. | 52G closed. |
| 10 | Initial load pickup (minimum load block and hold **[TBC]**), then ramp to the setpoint at the OEM loading rate **[TBC]**. | Load setpoint reached. |

### 1.4 Critical speed band handling
- The governor must not hold or dwell setpoints in 1600–1900 rpm.
- Any speed setpoint or hold request inside the band is rejected, and the ramp continues through to the next valid setpoint.
- The 500 rpm and 2000 rpm holds are both outside the band.
- If the ramp stalls in the band (for example loss of steam flow), the DCS raises an alarm after a timeout **[TBC]**. The operator must either continue the ramp or take a controlled shutdown, because holding in the band is not allowed.

### 1.5 Sequence aborts
- Any trip in section 2 sends the sequence to the tripped state.
- Alarm conditions during a hold (vibration ≥ 75 µm, thrust ≥ ±0.4 mm) pause the sequence and stop the hold timer from advancing. They do not trip.
- A pause during acceleration freezes the ramp. It does not hold in the critical band: if the turbine is in the band, the ramp continues, or the operator trips.
- After a trip, the rotor must go onto the turning gear at zero speed. The restart rules (cold/warm) are based on the rotor's thermal state **[TBC]**.

## 2. Protection

### 2.1 Lube oil pressure (PT-210)

| Condition | Setpoint | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Normal | 1.5 barg | None. |
| Low | < 1.0 barg | Auto-start P-11 (if not running), alarm. |
| Low-low | < 0.7 barg | Auto-start P-12, alarm. |
| Trip | 0.6 barg | Turbine trip. |

- The thresholds are close together (0.1 barg between P-12 start and trip). Use three transmitters (2oo3 voting) for the trip function and separate transmitters for the auto-starts **[TBC]**. A single PT-210 would make a spurious trip or a missed trip too likely.
- Apply short filtering or delay only if the OEM allows it. Do not delay the trip.
- The P-12 start logic must be hardwired to DC supply and independent of the DCS.
- Trip on low oil pressure must be active from turbine roll-off, not only at rated speed.
- Tripping on oil pressure while the rotor coasts down requires P-12 (or P-11) to keep running until the rotor is stopped. The pumps must not be stopped on trip.
- A defined bypass/inhibit during startup is permitted only if the OEM specifies it. Otherwise there is none.

### 2.2 Overspeed
- Electronic overspeed trip at 110% (3960 rpm) in the Woodward, with 2oo3 speed probes **[TBC]**. It acts on the trip/stop valve solenoids directly.
- The mechanical overspeed bolt is set at 111% (3996 rpm) and is the independent backup. The electronic trip must act first, with only 36 rpm between them. The settings and test procedure must keep them separate.
- Overspeed tests: electronic test and mechanical bolt test procedures **[TBC]**. The mechanical test must use a controlled, supervised overspeed procedure.
- Generator breaker trip on loss of load, so that the governor sees a rejection event and controls speed.

### 2.3 Shaft vibration (XT-301/302)
- Alarm at 75 µm.
- Trip at 125 µm, voted 2oo2 per bearing (both probes of the bearing must exceed it).
- A 2oo2 vote means one failed or drifting probe cannot trip, but it also means a single probe seeing a real fault will not trip. Consider adding a probe-fault alarm and a rule that one probe above the trip level for more than a set time raises a high-priority alarm **[TBC]**.
- Because 2oo2 hides a faulted probe, probe health (signal range check) must raise an alarm.
- During critical band passage, vibration will rise. Confirm with the OEM whether the trip should be kept at 125 µm or modified during acceleration **[TBC]**. Do not mask the trip without OEM approval.

### 2.4 Axial thrust position (ZT-310)
- Alarm at ±0.4 mm.
- Trip at ±0.6 mm.
- The voting logic is not specified. Recommend 2oo3 on three probes **[TBC]**, or 2oo2 if two probes are provided, matching the vibration approach.
- Probe-fault alarm on bad signal quality.

### 2.5 Loss of vacuum (PT-220)
- Trip at high exhaust pressure of 0.3 bara.
- Alarm setpoint below the trip **[TBC]**.
- Recommend 2oo3 voting **[TBC]**.
- The trip is armed once steam is admitted. During start, vacuum must be established first (permissive 6). Any start-up inhibit of this trip is permitted only if the OEM states it.
- On trip, also close extraction/bleed non-return valves and isolate steam to the gland seals per the OEM **[TBC]**.

### 2.6 Trip actions (common)
On any trip:
1. Close the trip/stop valve and control valves (trip solenoid de-energized, fail-safe).
2. Open generator breaker 52G (tripped by the turbine trip, with reverse-power supervision for a normal shutdown **[TBC]**).
3. Keep P-11/P-12 running for coast-down.
4. Engage the turning gear at zero speed (auto, only at zero speed).
5. First-out annunciation in the DCS. Trip reset requires the condition to be cleared and the turbine to be at a safe state.

### 2.7 Turning gear interlocks
- M-15 can be engaged only at zero speed (zero-speed switch or speed probes at 0 rpm).
- M-15 is not allowed to start if oil pressure is below normal.
- If M-15 stops during turning on a hot rotor, raise an alarm. The OEM shall define the response (rotor bow risk) **[TBC]**.

## 3. Items to resolve before issue
1. Transmitter counts and voting for PT-210, ZT-310, PT-220, and speed.
2. Acceleration and loading rates, plus the critical-pass rate.
3. Warm and hot start rules, and the casing temperature criteria.
4. Alarm setpoints for PT-220.
5. M-15 disengage method.
6. Whether any trips are inhibited during the start sequence.
7. Test and proof-test intervals, and the SIL/safety requirements for the trip loops, if applicable.
